messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] customer=borealis-fintech region=eu-west-1 pool=dedicated-borealis-1 metric=p99_latency value=1450ms SLO=600ms — paging on-call
sarah.ops: paging @ian-oncall — Borealis Fintech dedicated pool in eu-west hitting p99 > 1.4s. Customer on dedicated reserved capacity, high business impact.
ian-oncall: on it. pulling logs + heatmap. any recent deploys?
priya-eng: no prod deploys in eu-west in the last 30m. looking at request distribution now.
marco-runtime: I see a KV cache miss surge for that pool starting ~14:03 UTC. Could be cache eviction thrash.
emily-csm: looping in CSM and AM. Borealis team is actively experiencing slow responses in their payments flow. They just pinged their SRE.
dan-support: confirm customer seeing errors or just latency? their dashboard shows increased timeouts in retrying calls.
sarah.ops: customer reported increased end-to-end timeouts and retries at 14:05 UTC. no 5xx spikes on platform, mainly long tail latency.
ian-oncall: grabbing call traces. attaching sample tail: ```trace_id=abc123 p99=1620ms path=/v1/generate model=redwood-large prompt_len=180```. looks like long generation times.
marco-runtime: check GPU utilization on dedicated pool: `rbctl pool describe dedicated-borealis-1 --region eu-west-1`
priya-eng: GPU utilization 98% on two nodes, NVLink queues full, async IO backlog. Also a tenant in the pool has a sudden traffic spike — but it seems to be Borealis (single-tenant).
ian-oncall: is this the customer workload or a noisy tenant sharing the pool? they have reserved capacity but burst policy might let other tenants in?
marco-runtime: confirmed pool is isolated to Borealis account IDs. No other tenants. so traffic spike is their own.
emily-csm: Borealis confirms they kicked off a bulk reconciliation job at 14:00 UTC. They didn't expect this to hit inference tier but it does.
sarah.ops: immediate mitigation options: 1) apply rate limit to Borealis (soft throttle) 2) spin up additional dedicated nodes in eu-west warm pool 3) fallback route to a compatible lower-cost/quantized model variant 4) engage account for job scheduling.
priya-eng: quick wins: enable model-variant fallback + reduce max_tokens for that customer route. fallback should reduce per-token latency.
marco-runtime: I can enable fallback via routing policy — will take ~30s. Command: ```rbctl routing update --pool dedicated-borealis-1 --fallback redwood-medium-quant --enable```.
ian-oncall: go for fallback + reduce concurrency per connection to limit queue depth. Patch in gateway: ```/config/routes/borealis.json" set \"max_concurrency\":2, \"max_tokens\":256```
ian-oncall: applying now...
deploy-bot: [deploy] routing-policy-update to dedicated-borealis-1 started by ian-oncall at 14:12 UTC
deploy-bot: [deploy] routing-policy-update SUCCEEDED (id: dp-8843)
marco-runtime: fallback active. monitoring tail latencies.
priya-eng: seeing p99 drop to ~700ms within 60s, p95 already near 250ms. Great.
emily-csm: updating Borealis: we have a temporary routing fallback enabled and are throttling heavy jobs. asking them to pause the reconciliation job if possible.
emily-csm: Borealis SRE says they can pause the job ~15m from now but need to finish by EOD; are we okay to keep fallback on for an hour?
ian-oncall: fine for now. we need to ensure no correctness regressions — ask product to confirm tolerances for quantized model.
priya-eng: quick quality check run against a small prompt set shows acceptable variance; documented.
sarah.ops: next, scale plan: if they cannot pause, we need to add one more GPU node to the dedicated pool. Marco estimate ~7-9min to boot and warm.
marco-runtime: initiating scale-up: `rbctl pool scale dedicated-borealis-1 +1 --region eu-west-1`
deploy-bot: [scale] pool-scale initiated (task id sc-9921)
marco-runtime: new node joined at 14:21 UTC, warming kv-cache. p99 now ~320ms.
ian-oncall: ongoing monitoring. marking customer impact degraded but functional. creating SLO breach update in incident tracker.
sarah.ops: incident severity = sev2 (customer SLO breach, partial degradation). notifying account team.
emily-csm: AM on call notified, on customer bridge. Borealis wants postmortem and runbook update.
dan-support: logging timeline and adding tickets: INF-2319 (runbook), CUST-4572 (account follow-up).
priya-eng: action item: add explicit limits for tenant-initiated background jobs that hit inference tier for dedicated customers (runbook + API guidance).
ian-oncall: handoff to night shift in 45m. I'll prep a short handoff note: current mitigation = fallback enabled, pool scaled +1, p99 stabilized ~300ms, watch kv-cache miss rate and queue length.\sarah.ops: Ian — please include commands to rollback fallback and how to verify model parity.
ian-oncall: handoff note prepared: "Fallback=redwood-medium-quant active; to rollback: `rbctl routing update --pool dedicated-borealis-1 --fallback none --disable` then verify p99 < 600ms for 10m and run test prompts. Monitor `rbctl metrics tail dedicated-borealis-1 --metric p99_latency`".
marco-runtime: added dashboard alert: KV_CACHE_MISS_RATE > 0.2 for 3m -> paging to eng-runtime.
emily-csm: capturing customer impact: estimated affected requests ~12k, retries increased, customer revenue risk flagged; AM will discuss credits.
sarah.ops: final check — any lasting errors? 5xx remain <0.1% and not correlated.
ian-oncall: no major errors. moving to monitoring state.
ian-oncall: handing off to @priya-eng for overnight coverage. I will post this thread summary in #incidents-ops and attach to incident tracker.
priya-eng: taking over. I will keep fallback in place until Borealis confirms job paused, or until we validate stable p99 for 2 hours.
sarah.ops: thanks all. follow-ups: 1) INF-2319 runbook updates 2) platform change to surface tenant job-to-inference mappings 3) update SLA doc for dedicated pools to include guidance on heavy batch jobs.
emily-csm: I scheduled post-incident call with Borealis for tomorrow 09:00 UTC.
dan-support: closing immediate page — monitoring in 30m windows.
incident-bot: incident updated: sev=2 -> state=mitigated -> assignees=[ian-oncall, priya-eng]
ian-oncall: wrap: p99 restored to target after scale+fallback. handing off logs/trace artifacts and Q/A notes in the ticket.
priya-eng: acknowledged. I'll publish a short postmortem draft after the morning triage.
notes: post-incident: confirm billing adjustments separately. ensure runbook has explicit steps for dedicated pool scale and fallback rollback.
